plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Clouds of blush-white blossoms cover bare branches before the leaves appear. Each flower is five-petaled and lightly almond-scented. Petals drift down like snow in the spring breeze.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early April in Tokyo and much of central Japan, with peak bloom often around the turn of the month
plants.location: Japan, especially Tokyo, Kyoto and the Honshu lowlands
plants.funFact: Japan's cherry blossom forecast tracks the Yoshino cherry. Its trees are mostly clones grafted from a single original, so they tend to bloom in near-perfect unison.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Nodding golden trumpets rise from a paler ring of petals above blue-green, strap-like leaves. In woodlands and meadows they gather into drifts of yellow. They are a cheerful sign that winter is ending.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April in the UK and western Europe
plants.location: Woodlands and meadows of England, Wales and western Europe
plants.funFact: Daffodil bulbs contain alkaloids such as galantamine. This compound has been developed into a medicine for Alzheimer's disease, and the same toxins make the plants unappealing to grazing animals.

plants.name: Eschscholzia californica
plants.description: Silky, cup-shaped flowers glow like molten gold across hillsides and roadsides. The petals open in full sun and close on cloudy days and at night. Feathery blue-green foliage sets off the blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late February to September, with spectacular mass blooms in March and April in wet years
plants.funFact: California's state flower can bloom so densely that superblooms are visible from space. Its petals fold shut when it is cold or overcast, which protects the pollen.
